space.hint: Space: click its corners, then double-click or press Enter, and name it. Esc cancels.
space.name.title: Name the space
space.name: Space name
space.name.need: Type a name for the space.

space.added.=0: Added the space {name}. No markups are in it yet.
space.added.one: Added the space {name}: {n} markup is in it.
space.added.other: Added the space {name}: {n} markups are in it.

space.go.title: Show the space {name}
sketch.label: Length of the next segment
sketch.title: Type a length such as 12'6" or 3.5 m, and optionally < and an angle in degrees (0 = right, 90 = up). Enter places the point, Esc closes.
sketch.placed: Placed a point {len} on. Type the next length, or click.
sketch.err.scale: Calibrate this sheet first: lengths are typed in its real units.
sketch.err.length: That is not a length. Type it like 12'6", 12.5 or 3.5 m.
sketch.err.angle: The angle after < is not a number of degrees.
sketch.err.direction: Move the pointer the way the segment should go, or type an angle after <.
col.button.title: Your own columns on markups: text, a choice, a number or a date
col.title: Custom columns
col.text: Columns you add show in every markup's Properties, in the list (filter and sort by them) and in the CSV and XLSX exports. They are saved with the PDF.
col.name: Column name
col.err.name: Give every column a name.
col.err.choices: A choice column needs at least one choice.
sort.label: Sort
photo.add.title: Add a photo to the thread (on a tablet, take one); what you typed above becomes its caption
photo.title: Photo
nav.view_cw.title: Turn the view a quarter turn clockwise (the PDF itself does not change)
nav.view_ccw.title: Turn the view a quarter turn counterclockwise (the PDF itself does not change)
view.rotated: The view is turned {n}° for this sheet; the PDF is unchanged. New text reads upright as you see it.
view.rotated.none: The view is back the way the PDF is.
compare.lines.busy: Comparing the lines of the two sheets…
compare.lines.none: These sheets have no lines to compare (scans): use the picture overlay.
compare.lines.done: Red: {removed} pt of lines only on the old sheet. Blue: {added} pt only on the new one.
compare.cloud.title: Draw a revision cloud round each group of changed lines on the new sheet, as one step you can undo
legend.title: Legend
legend.add.title: Put a legend on this sheet that lists each kind of markup with how many there are; it keeps counting as you work
legend.added: Legend added at the top right. Move and resize it like any markup; it counts as you go.
batch.need: Select the markups to copy first.
batch.title: Copy to other sheets

batch.text.one: Put a copy of the selected markup in the same place on each sheet you tick, such as a stamp on every sheet of an issue.
batch.text.other: Put copies of the {n} selected markups in the same place on each sheet you tick.

setcmp.note: Pair every sheet of an old issue with the sheet of the same number in the new one, see which changed most, and cloud the changes on all of them.
setcmp.need: Pick two different open files: the old issue and the new one.
setcmp.none: No sheet numbers match between the two files. Name the sheets first (Rename sheet), or compare sheet by sheet above.

setcmp.done.one: {n} sheet paired; {changed} changed. Most changed first:
setcmp.done.other: {n} sheets paired; {changed} changed. Most changed first:

undo.setcmp.cloud: Cloud the changes in the set
bm.h.title: The bookmarks (outline) of the open sheet's PDF: follow, rename, remove, or build them from the sheet names; saved with the PDF
bm.nowhere: This bookmark does not point at a page of this file.
bm.rename.title: Rename bookmark
bm.title.label: Bookmark title
bm.build.title: Build bookmarks from the sheets

bm.build.replace.one: This replaces the file's {n} bookmark with one per sheet, named as the sheets list shows them.
bm.build.replace.other: This replaces the file's {n} bookmarks with one per sheet, named as the sheets list shows them.

bm.built.one: Built {n} bookmark. Save to keep them in the PDF.
bm.built.other: Built {n} bookmarks. Save to keep them in the PDF.

bm.add.title: Add a bookmark
live.status.reconnecting: Lost the connection to the live session. Reconnecting…
live.status.waiting: Waiting for the host to let you in…
live.ended: The live session ended. Your copy stays here, unsaved: save it to keep it.
live.refused: {what} was taken back: someone changed it first, or it no longer fits.
live.refused.locked: {what} was taken back: locked by the host.
live.refused.role: You can only look in this session: the host let you in as a viewer.
input.style.markupcraft.hint: MarkupCraft's own toolbar and single-letter tool keys: everything one click away.
input.style.review.hint: A menu bar (File, Edit, View, Document, Markup, Measure, Review, Window) over a row of review tools, with tool keys set out the way PDF review programs set theirs: H highlighter, Q callout, N polygon, Shift+T note, and the measurements on Alt+Shift (L length, A area, C count, K calibrate). The middle button pans; Space and drag still pans.
calc.err.end: The calculation ends too soon (character {pos}): a value is missing.
calc.err.extra: Something follows the end of the calculation at character {pos}: "{text}".
calc.err.deep: Too many brackets inside each other (character {pos}).
calc.err.long: That is too long to read (over {pos} characters).
calc.err.area: Two lengths multiplied make an area, not a length (character {pos}).
calc.err.ratio: A plain number divided by a length is not a length (character {pos}).
calc.err.function: No function called "{text}" (character {pos}). Use abs, round, ceil or floor.
calc.err.not_positive: The length must be more than zero.
calc.err.number: The result is not a number (character {pos}).
tool.content.title: Page content: select and change the page's own lines, pictures and text, not markups (B)
base.blocked.encrypted: This PDF is encrypted, so its page content can't be changed here. Markups still work.
base.blocked.signed: This PDF is signed. Changing its page content would break the signature, so MarkupCraft leaves it as it is. Markups still work.
base.blocked.unreadable: MarkupCraft can't read this page's content ({why}). Markups still work.
base.hint: Page content: click a line, picture or line of text to select it, drag it to move it, drag a corner to resize it. Double-click a line to move its points, or a line of text to change its words.
base.scan: This page is one picture (a scan): you can move, resize or delete the picture, but there are no lines or words in it to edit.
base.empty: Nothing on this page can be picked with these kinds turned on.
base.points.title: Move the line's points and curve handles (or double-click the line)
base.points.hint: Drag a point or a curve handle. Esc, or a click away from the line, ends point editing.
base.points.none: This one has no points to move here: resize it with the corners of its box.
base.reset.sheet: Put this page back as it was

base.changes.one: 1 change to this page's own content.
base.changes.other: {n} changes to this page's own content.

base.note: These edits change the page itself in the copy you save; markups stay separate. Lines, pictures and lines of text the PDF draws can be moved, resized, recolored or deleted. A scanned page is one picture: what is in the picture can't be edited.
base.none: Nothing there to pick (the kinds under Pick decide what can be picked).
base.refused.clip: That line clips other content: moving it would change what they show, so it stays as it is.
base.refused.across-streams: That object is split between two parts of the page's content, so MarkupCraft leaves it as it is.
base.refused.text: Color and line width can't be changed on lines drawn inside text.
base.refused.flat: That object is squashed flat in the file, so it can't be moved or resized.
base.refused.font: That text's font can't be written to here.
base.refused.gone: That object is no longer on the page.
base.refused.shading: A color blend fills its whole area, so it can't be moved on its own.
base.refused.other: That edit can't be written into this page ({why}).

base.save.refused.one: 1 page edit could not be written and was left out.
base.save.refused.other: {n} page edits could not be written and were left out.

base.rebuild.failed: The page could not be redrawn with its edits: {error}
base.into.title: Make these markups part of the page's own content (line work only: no text, pictures or see-through color)
base.into.cant: Only line work can go into the page: text, pictures, stamps and see-through colors stay markups.

base.into.done.one: 1 markup is part of the page now (Ctrl+Z takes it back).
base.into.done.other: {n} markups are part of the page now (Ctrl+Z takes them back).

base.picture.replace.title: Put another picture (PNG or JPEG) in this one's place; its proportions are kept inside the same box
base.picture.bad: That file is not a PNG or JPEG picture MarkupCraft can use.
base.refused.picture: That picture could not be replaced in this file.
base.text.done: Words changed, in the line's own font.
base.text.fallback: Words changed. The file's copy of {font} has no {letters}, so those letters are printed in Helvetica.
base.text.font.subset: Font: {font}. The file carries only some of its letters ({letters}); others are printed in Helvetica.
base.refused.metrics: MarkupCraft doesn't have this font's letter widths (a standard font the file doesn't describe), so it can't place new words in it.
pic.paste.label: Pasted picture
pic.paste.done: Picture pasted as a markup: drag it into place, or resize it by its corners.
pic.paste.bad: That clipboard picture is not a PNG or JPEG MarkupCraft can use.
pic.paste.none: There is no picture on the clipboard.
pic.paste.denied: The browser did not let MarkupCraft read the clipboard. Press Ctrl+V instead (⌘V on a Mac).
pic.paste.no_api: This browser can't read pictures from the clipboard from a menu. Press Ctrl+V instead (⌘V on a Mac).
rec.note: RFIs, submittals and daily logs, each tied to a sheet and, for RFIs and submittals, a place on it. They are saved inside the PDF, work without a network, and join another copy of the set by their ids (Merge).
rec.bcf.title: Export the listed records as BCF topics, each with a snapshot of its place on the sheet
rec.merge.title: Join the records of another copy of this PDF (for example from a tablet that worked offline) into this set
rec.empty: No records yet. Add an RFI, a submittal or a daily log.
rec.title: Title
rec.sheet.gone: Sheet not in the open files
rec.attach.name: Attachment name
rec.attach.placeholder: File name, for example 03-30-00 mix design.pdf
rec.attach.note: Only the names are kept, so the list tells the team what goes with this record. The files stay where they are.
rec.reply.label: Reply
rec.remove.title: Remove {no}?
rec.remove.text: The record leaves the list and the saved PDF. If another copy still has it, a merge will know it was removed here.
rec.place.new: Tap or click the sheet where the {type} belongs. Esc cancels.
rec.place.move: Tap or click the sheet where the pin should go. Esc cancels.

rec.bcf.done.one: Exported 1 record as a BCF topic.

rcsv.title: Title
rcsv.author: Author
input.cmd.markups.bcf: Export the markups as BCF issues
input.cmd.punch.add: Add the selection to the punch list
input.cmd.chest.save: Save the selection as a tool
input.style.ribbon.hint: A ribbon of tabs named for the work (Mark up, Measure, Edit, Review, Pages, View) with a File menu and quick buttons, and MarkupCraft's own one-letter keys. The workspace layouts build their ribbon from it.
ws.browser.hint: Click a sheet to open it in a tab. The markups list follows its filters.
ws.opt.open: Open a PDF or start blank pages.
ws.opt.pick: Click a markup to select it, or pick a tool.
ws.failed: The workspace layout could not start ({reason}); the classic layout is in use.
